title: Why the Terminal password prompt shows nothing when you type
summary: When Terminal asks for your password, it does not show dots, stars or letters while you type. This is normal: the characters are hidden on purpose, so the input is not broken.

steps.explain: When a command needs administrator rights, Terminal shows a prompt such as 'Password:' and waits. sudo reads the password from the terminal without showing it, so nothing appears on the line while you type. This is by design and does not mean the keyboard is broken.
Type your Mac login password exactly and press Return. Your typing is still received even though no dots, stars or letters appear.
If the password is wrong, sudo prints a message such as 'Sorry, try again.' and asks you once more. If it is right, the command runs and the cursor moves to a new line.
Sometimes no prompt appears at all. sudo keeps a short-lived record of a recent successful password for this Terminal window, so it runs the command straight away. This is normal and is not an error.
The same rule applies to any Terminal command that asks for your Mac login password. The password fields in System Settings and on the login screen do show dots, which is a different kind of field.
